title.rendered: Love: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 1

excerpt.rendered: Classical Greek had multiple words for love. When the New Testament wanted to describe the love that flows into a believer’s life by the Holy Spirit, it reached past all of them and chose a word that was almost forgotten. Agapē.

content.rendered:
Classical Greek had multiple words for love. Eros for romantic desire. Philia for the affection of friends. Storge for the bond of family. When the New Testament wanted to describe the love that flows into a believer’s life by the Holy Spirit, it reached past all of them and chose a word that was almost forgotten. Agapē.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, September 24, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 1

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Classical Greek was one of the richest languages in the ancient world for describing love. There was eros, the word for romantic desire and passion. There was philia, the word for the deep affection between friends. There was storge, the word for the natural bond between parents and children. Each word carried a specific and useful meaning, and each was well-used in the literature of the day. But when the writers of the New Testament wanted to describe the love of God, and the love that flows into a believer’s life by the Holy Spirit, they reached past every one of those words and chose a word that had almost fallen out of use in ordinary Greek. Agapē. A love that no eros, no philia, no storge could quite carry.

Agapē is the love of the will, not merely the feelings. It is chosen, not merely fallen into. It is directed toward the good of the other, regardless of what the other gives back. It is the love that flows one direction, from the giver to the receiver, without needing to be replenished by anything the receiver contributes. It is the love with which the Father loved a rebellious world enough to send His Son. It is the love with which the Son loved the disciples enough to wash their feet on the night before the cross. It is the love with which the Holy Spirit is now filling every believer who will yield to His work. And when Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22, he places agapē first, because every other fruit that follows it is a form of it.

The Passion Translation opens up the depth of what the Spirit produces: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action, a life full of virtue, faith that prevails, gentleness of heart, and strength of spirit” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Notice how the Passion Translation reads the whole list. Divine love in all its varied expressions. Joy is love overflowing. Peace is love subduing. Patience is love enduring. Kindness is love in action. Every other fruit is an expression of the first one. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love” (Galatians 5:22 AMPC). The work which His presence within accomplishes. Not the work the believer manufactures with willpower. The work the Spirit produces where He is welcomed to work.

This is why the New Testament is so insistent that agapē is not something a Christian generates. Paul writes in Romans 5:5 that “the love of God has been poured out in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who was given to us.” Poured out. Past tense. Already done. The love the Christian is called to walk in is not a love the Christian has to work up. It is a love the Christian has to yield to. The Spirit has already filled the reservoir. The believer’s part is to let it flow out toward the people the Father puts in their path.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the first fruit and the parent of every other fruit. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if there is a person in your life you cannot naturally love, you do not need to manufacture affection you do not feel. You need to yield to the love the Holy Spirit has already poured into your heart, and let it flow to that person, regardless of what they give back. That is agapē. It is not a technique. It is not a performance. It is a fruit. And the Spirit is producing it in every believer who will stay rooted in Christ. Let Him produce it in you today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that agapē is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Not a love I manufacture with willpower. Not a love that depends on what the other person gives back. A love You have already poured into my heart by Your Spirit, waiting to flow out toward the people You put in my path. Today I yield to that love. I stop trying to produce it. I let You produce it in me. And I let it flow to the person I would not naturally love. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Agapē is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. The love of God has been poured into my heart. I do not manufacture it. I yield to it. And I let it flow to the people the Father puts in my path.
